title: The OpenROAD Project: Unleashing Hardware Innovation
object_controlled: the translation from placed logic to routed and checked physical design
constraint: digital implementation requires timing, routing, power, and manufacturability evidence, not only a synthesized netlist
mathematical_form: graph placement, routing resource allocation, timing inequalities, and constrained optimization
concrete_method: integrate placement, clocking, routing, timing analysis, and design repair into an open flow
evidence_artifact: generated layout artifacts, timing reports, routed design checks, and reproducible flow scripts
failure_boundary: a flow result is not production signoff unless the process setup, rule decks, extraction, timing, and manufacturing checks are strong enough

title: OpenLane: An Automated RTL-to-GDSII Flow
object_controlled: the sequence of tool decisions that turns RTL into a manufacturable layout candidate
constraint: each translation can preserve logic while breaking timing, routing, power, design rules, or extraction behavior
mathematical_form: sequential constrained optimization with verification gates after each representation change
concrete_method: compose synthesis, floorplanning, placement, routing, extraction, DRC, LVS, and timing checks into a repeatable flow
evidence_artifact: flow logs, DEF/GDS outputs, timing reports, DRC/LVS status, and extracted views
failure_boundary: automation can hide incorrect assumptions when constraints, PDK setup, or signoff checks are incomplete

title: A Graph Placement Methodology for Fast Chip Design
object_controlled: placement coordinates for macros and standard-cell regions
constraint: good placement must balance wire length, congestion, timing, power delivery, and later routability
mathematical_form: policy search over graph embeddings with reward from physical design proxies
concrete_method: learn placement decisions from design graphs and evaluate candidates with downstream physical metrics
evidence_artifact: placement quality metrics, wirelength, congestion estimates, timing proxies, and comparison against tool baselines
failure_boundary: a learned placement is weak if proxy reward improves while routed timing or manufacturability gets worse

title: Machine Learning for Electronic Design Automation: A Survey
object_controlled: the choice of where learning methods fit into the design toolchain
constraint: EDA tasks differ by checker strength, data availability, cost of evaluation, and tolerance for wrong suggestions
mathematical_form: task decomposition across prediction, search, optimization, and classification loops
concrete_method: organize learning methods by EDA stage and by the artifact they predict or optimize
evidence_artifact: task comparisons, benchmark results, tool-stage mappings, and limits of available datasets
failure_boundary: a survey taxonomy is not design evidence unless each task has a checker and a measurable engineering outcome

title: Bayesian Optimization Approach for Analog Circuit Synthesis Using Neural Network
object_controlled: device sizes and bias points under gain, bandwidth, power, noise, and stability constraints
constraint: SPICE evaluations are expensive and the design surface is coupled and nonlinear
mathematical_form: sequential optimization under expensive noisy measurements
concrete_method: use a surrogate model to choose promising circuit parameters and update the model after each simulation
evidence_artifact: SPICE-measured objective values, constraint satisfaction, sample count, and comparison with manual or sweep baselines
failure_boundary: a found sizing point can fail after layout extraction, corners, mismatch, or unmodeled operating conditions

title: DREAMPlace: Deep Learning Toolkit-Enabled GPU Acceleration for Modern VLSI Placement
object_controlled: standard-cell placement coordinates under wirelength, density, timing, and routability pressure
constraint: modern placement needs high-quality optimization over millions of movable objects while keeping density and physical constraints under control
mathematical_form: analytical placement cast as an optimization problem similar to neural-network training on GPU tensors
concrete_method: formulate placement objectives and gradients in a deep-learning framework so GPU acceleration can speed global placement
evidence_artifact: placement quality, runtime, wirelength, density behavior, and comparisons with established placement baselines
failure_boundary: faster global placement is not enough if detailed placement, routing, extracted timing, or congestion evidence fails later

title: ABC: A System for Sequential Synthesis and Verification
object_controlled: binary sequential logic represented for optimization, mapping, and verification
constraint: logic transformations must improve implementation while preserving the intended sequential behavior
mathematical_form: graph rewriting and equivalence reasoning over And-Inverter Graphs and sequential state
concrete_method: use a common logic representation and transformation engine for synthesis, technology mapping, and verification tasks
evidence_artifact: optimized networks, equivalence results, verification outcomes, and synthesis/mapping reports
failure_boundary: logic equivalence evidence does not prove physical timing, power, routing, or analog behavior after implementation

title: The VTR Project: Architecture and CAD for FPGAs from Verilog to Routing
subtheme: FPGA architecture and CAD research flow
object_controlled: the mapping from Verilog logic into an FPGA architecture with packing, placement, routing, and timing analysis
constraint: FPGA CAD must respect both the user's circuit and the target architecture's programmable resources
mathematical_form: technology mapping, packing, graph placement, routing-resource allocation, and timing analysis over configurable fabric
concrete_method: provide an open research flow that takes Verilog and architecture descriptions through synthesis, packing, placement, routing, and timing
evidence_artifact: placed-and-routed FPGA designs, timing reports, benchmark results, and architecture exploration outputs
failure_boundary: a CAD research flow can compare architectures and algorithms without proving commercial device readiness or ASIC manufacturability

title: ALIGN: A System for Automating Analog Layout
object_controlled: the translation from SPICE netlist to layout geometry under analog matching and design-rule constraints
constraint: analog layout must preserve hierarchy, symmetry, matching, parasitics, and manufacturability while moving from schematic intent to GDSII
mathematical_form: hierarchical block assembly under geometric, electrical, and design-rule constraints
concrete_method: detect netlist hierarchy, generate parameterized cells, and assemble blocks under layout constraints to produce GDSII
evidence_artifact: generated layouts for analog circuit families, GDSII output, design-rule handling, and comparison with intended netlists
failure_boundary: automatic analog layout can fail if extracted parasitics, matching, symmetry, or process-specific design rules are not strong enough

title: MAGICAL: Toward Fully Automated Analog IC Layout Leveraging Human and Machine Intelligence
object_controlled: analog placement and routing decisions that preserve circuit-level intent after layout
constraint: analog layout depends on human layout knowledge about symmetry, matching, proximity, routing, and parasitic control
mathematical_form: layout synthesis as constrained placement and routing with learned or encoded analog design patterns
concrete_method: combine rule-based and machine-intelligence-guided steps to automate analog layout generation
evidence_artifact: generated analog layouts, runtime reduction, layout quality, and circuit-specific comparison against manual or baseline flows
failure_boundary: automation remains weak if it cannot explain or verify the analog reasons behind placement, matching, and routing choices

title: ChipNeMo: Domain-Adapted LLMs for Chip Design
subtheme: domain-adapted language models for chip engineering
object_controlled: language-heavy chip design work such as engineering assistance, script generation, retrieval, and triage
constraint: general language models lack chip-specific vocabulary, design context, proprietary corpus knowledge, and tool-flow grounding
mathematical_form: domain adaptation through tokenizer changes, continued pretraining, instruction tuning, retrieval, and task-specific evaluation
concrete_method: adapt an LLM to chip design data and evaluate it on chip-design assistant, EDA scripting, and engineering tasks
evidence_artifact: task evaluations, domain adaptation ablations, retrieval effects, and comparisons against general-purpose models
failure_boundary: a chip LLM is not design evidence unless its output is checked by compilers, simulators, EDA tools, or expert review

title: VerilogEval: Evaluating Large Language Models for Verilog Code Generation
object_controlled: functional correctness of generated Verilog against executable test problems
constraint: fluent RTL-looking text can compile incorrectly, simulate incorrectly, or fail corner cases even when it appears plausible
mathematical_form: benchmark evaluation as generated program compared against golden behavior through simulation tests
concrete_method: use HDLBits-style Verilog tasks and automated functional checks to evaluate model-generated hardware code
evidence_artifact: pass rates, simulation outputs, compiler failures, task categories, and fine-tuning comparisons
failure_boundary: passing benchmark tasks does not prove timing closure, physical implementation, CDC correctness, reset safety, or design intent coverage

title: Power Distribution Network Generation for Optimizing IR-Drop Aware Timing
object_controlled: supply voltage delivered through the on-chip power distribution network
constraint: current through resistive power metal causes voltage drop that can slow gates, break timing, and reduce reliability
mathematical_form: PDN refinement as constrained optimization over power-grid geometry, current demand, voltage drop, and timing impact
concrete_method: generate a refined power distribution network from an initial PDN while optimizing IR-drop-aware timing behavior
evidence_artifact: IR-drop reports, timing impact, generated PDN geometry, and comparison against baseline power-grid choices
failure_boundary: a power grid can look adequate before activity, package effects, dynamic switching, and electromigration are checked

title: Encoder-Decoder Networks for Analyzing Thermal and Power Delivery Networks
subtheme: surrogate analysis for power, thermal, and reliability signoff
object_controlled: predicted voltage drop, electromigration risk, and temperature fields across a chip
constraint: full PDN and thermal analysis is computationally expensive but needed to catch power and reliability failures
mathematical_form: field prediction as image-to-image or sequence-to-sequence approximation of PDE-like analysis
concrete_method: train encoder-decoder networks to predict IR drop, electromigration hotspots, and thermal maps from design patterns
evidence_artifact: prediction error against commercial tools, runtime speedup, hotspot classification, and transfer across related designs
failure_boundary: a fast surrogate is unsafe if it misses rare hotspots, package effects, workload spikes, or design cases outside its training distribution

title: Forecasting Cost and Yield
object_controlled: expected cost per good die as yield improves over manufacturing time
constraint: early production has uncertain defect behavior, learning rate, demand, and process maturity
mathematical_form: yield and cost modeled as learning curves over manufacturing time and production experience
concrete_method: simulate yield learning and cost trajectories to compare manufacturing strategies and product ramps
evidence_artifact: forecast yield curves, cost curves, process-learning assumptions, and scenario comparisons
failure_boundary: yield forecasts fail when defect mechanisms, product mix, process changes, or test coverage differ from the model assumptions

title: LegUp: An Open-Source High-Level Synthesis Tool for FPGA-Based Processor/Accelerator Systems
subtheme: high-level synthesis from software to hardware
object_controlled: the translation from C program behavior into hardware accelerators and processor-connected logic
constraint: higher-level code must become hardware with explicit concurrency, memory movement, interfaces, timing, and area cost
mathematical_form: program dependence and scheduling transformed into hardware datapaths, control logic, and resource allocation
concrete_method: compile standard C into FPGA hardware accelerators connected to a processor system and compare quality of results
evidence_artifact: generated hardware, FPGA implementation metrics, performance and area results, and comparison against commercial HLS tools
failure_boundary: HLS can hide hardware costs if memory traffic, scheduling, timing, and interfaces are not inspected after synthesis

title: Statistical Timing Analysis: From Basic Principles to State of the Art
object_controlled: probability distribution of path delays under process and environmental variation
constraint: deterministic timing corners can be too pessimistic or too weak when delay varies across devices and conditions
mathematical_form: path delay modeled as random variables with correlations and propagated through timing graph operations
concrete_method: survey statistical static timing analysis models that estimate timing behavior under variation
evidence_artifact: timing distributions, model assumptions, correlation handling, and comparison of SSTA approaches
failure_boundary: statistical timing is unsafe when variation models, correlations, or rare tail events do not match silicon behavior

title: The Survey of Chiplet-Based Integrated Architecture: An EDA Perspective
subtheme: chiplet architecture and advanced packaging EDA
object_controlled: partitioning, communication, physical integration, and reliability of multi-die chiplet systems
constraint: chiplets trade monolithic die limits for package-level communication, thermal, reliability, test, and cost constraints
mathematical_form: system partitioning and package integration as multi-objective optimization over cost, bandwidth, latency, yield, and reliability
concrete_method: survey EDA methods for chiplet architecture design, partitioning, integration, physical design, and reliability analysis
evidence_artifact: taxonomy of chiplet EDA tasks, method comparisons, architecture tradeoffs, and open challenges
failure_boundary: chiplet gains can disappear if interconnect, package yield, thermal behavior, testing, or ecosystem assumptions fail

title: Unleashing OpenTitan's Potential: A Silicon-Ready Embedded Secure Element for Root of Trust and Cryptographic Offloading
object_controlled: trusted hardware state for boot, keys, cryptographic acceleration, and secure SoC integration
constraint: a root of trust must preserve security boundaries while integrating memory, accelerators, buses, firmware, and system interfaces
mathematical_form: security architecture as state isolation, authenticated transitions, cryptographic workloads, and measured data movement
concrete_method: extend and integrate OpenTitan Earl Grey architecture for embedded root-of-trust and cryptographic offloading use cases
evidence_artifact: RTL-level architecture, integration methodology, cycle-accurate simulation, and cryptographic workload speedups
failure_boundary: performance improvement does not prove security unless threat model, isolation, verification, and side-channel boundaries are checked

title: A Survey of Hardware Trojan Taxonomy and Detection
subtheme: hardware security and malicious modification detection
object_controlled: trust that manufactured or integrated hardware has not been maliciously altered
constraint: small malicious changes can be rare, dormant, process-hidden, or activated only under special conditions
mathematical_form: taxonomy over insertion stage, physical form, activation trigger, payload action, and observable side effects
concrete_method: classify hardware Trojan types and survey detection methods including logic testing and side-channel analysis
evidence_artifact: threat taxonomy, detection-method comparison, trigger/payload classification, and limits of testing approaches
failure_boundary: detection is incomplete when triggers are rare, side-channel signals are masked by variation, or the threat model is too narrow

title: An analog-AI chip for energy-efficient speech recognition and transcription
object_controlled: the movement from programmed phase-change memory conductances to chip-level neural-network inference outputs
constraint: software-equivalent behavior requires device programming, tile communication, peripheral conversion, and digital control to preserve model computation under analog noise
mathematical_form: matrix-vector multiplication by conductance-weighted current summation with quantization, peripheral readout, and inter-tile activation movement
concrete_method: build a multi-tile analog AI chip using phase-change memory arrays and peripheral circuitry to run neural inference with measured chip-level throughput and accuracy
evidence_artifact: silicon measurements, model accuracy, sustained throughput per watt, tile count, memory-device count, and end-to-end inference demonstrations
failure_boundary: the chip result does not by itself solve transformer-scale LLM inference because attention, KV cache, long-context movement, adaptation, and precision boundaries remain separate constraints

title: Analog Foundation Models
subtheme: model adaptation for analog in-memory hardware
object_controlled: language-model behavior when weights and activations pass through noisy low-precision analog in-memory compute constraints
constraint: off-the-shelf LLMs lose accuracy when analog noise, input quantization, output quantization, and hardware-imposed precision limits change layer computations
mathematical_form: robust model adaptation under additive/multiplicative analog noise and constrained weight/input/output quantization
concrete_method: train or adapt foundation models with analog-hardware-aware constraints so model representations tolerate AIMC noise and quantization during inference
evidence_artifact: LLM benchmark results, comparison with low-bit digital baselines, noise and quantization ablations, and tested model families
failure_boundary: the method depends on simulated hardware assumptions and does not remove the need for real device calibration, converter limits, memory traffic, and chip-level scheduling evidence

title: Efficient Deployment of Transformer Models in Analog In-Memory Computing Hardware
subtheme: hybrid analog transformer deployment with digital adapters
object_controlled: transformer inference quality when dense layers are mapped to AIMC and compact digital adapters compensate for hardware constraints
constraint: analog tiles can carry dense projection work, but pretrained transformer layers are sensitive to noise, quantization, tile latency, and mismatch with the original computation
mathematical_form: low-rank residual adaptation around analog-approximated transformer projections with pipeline and latency balancing
concrete_method: deploy pretrained transformer layers on AIMC while using lightweight low-rank adapters in digital cores to recover accuracy without full hardware-aware retraining
evidence_artifact: accuracy recovery measurements, adapter overhead, latency modeling, pipeline analysis, and comparison against direct AIMC deployment
failure_boundary: digital adapters help only if the analog error is low-rank or locally correctable and if adapter latency and memory movement do not dominate decode

title: Analog In-Memory Computing Attention Mechanism for Fast and Energy-Efficient Large Language Models
subtheme: analog attention and writable token memory
object_controlled: attention dot products over token-dependent memory states during sequence generation
constraint: attention is not a fixed weight matrix; token states must be written, retained, read, and compared under analog memory nonidealities and context-window assumptions
mathematical_form: sliding-window self-attention dot products computed with charge or gain-cell analog memory and bounded by write/read noise and windowed context
concrete_method: use gain-cell analog in-memory structures to store recent token information and compute attention-related dot products with mixed-signal circuitry
evidence_artifact: architecture evaluation, attention workload mapping, energy or latency estimates, accuracy under nonidealities, and comparison with digital attention baselines
failure_boundary: the approach depends on attention-window assumptions and does not make the whole transformer analog because softmax, control, normalization, and output decisions remain digital-sensitive

title: Memory Is All You Need: An Overview of Compute-in-Memory Architectures for Accelerating Large Language Model Inference
object_controlled: the mapping of LLM inference operators, weights, activations, and KV-cache traffic onto compute-in-memory architecture choices
constraint: LLM inference is shaped by memory movement, prefill versus decode regimes, operator diversity, batch size, sequence length, and peripheral cost rather than matrix multiply alone
mathematical_form: operator and architecture taxonomy over memory traffic, compute placement, analog/digital CIM, attention structure, and system-level bottlenecks
concrete_method: survey CIM approaches for transformer inference and organize where each architecture can reduce movement or computation cost
evidence_artifact: taxonomy tables, operator mappings, architecture comparisons, workload analyses, and stated challenges for LLM inference
failure_boundary: a survey does not prove any one chip; each architecture still needs measured energy, latency, accuracy, converter, and memory-system evidence

title: AIHWKit Analog AI Hardware Simulation
subtheme: simulation of analog neural hardware nonidealities
object_controlled: software experiments that approximate analog in-memory hardware behavior before silicon is available
constraint: model claims are weak if device noise, drift, update limits, input/output quantization, and differential weight representation are not represented in simulation
mathematical_form: neural-network layers perturbed by analog tile models, device noise, drift, quantization, and training or inference compensation loops
concrete_method: provide software abstractions for analog tiles and device models so neural networks can be trained or evaluated under hardware-like nonidealities
evidence_artifact: simulated analog layer behavior, configurable device models, training/inference examples, and comparison against digital network behavior
failure_boundary: simulation is only as strong as the device and circuit assumptions; it must be checked against measured hardware before making chip-level claims
